clue.text: Pigs have returned to narrow ridge

parts.note: pigs are hogs
returned means came back, so it gives the word back

explanation.surface: A herd of pigs has wandered home along a narrow ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' looks like an instruction to reverse the pigs, but it simply supplies BACK, as in 'came back'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogsback is a geological term for a long, sharp-crested hill shaped like a pig's spine.

clue.text: Walk with difficulty — it's very black in the pit

indicators.note: very black is placed in the pit

parts.note: a pit is a hole
BB is the pencil grade for very black, soft lead

explanation.surface: Stumbling about in a pitch-dark mine.
explanation.walkthrough: BB is the pencil grading for very soft, very black lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobble is to limp or move awkwardly.

clue.text: Yellow plume from very small bird

parts.note: gold is a yellow colour
a crest is a plume or tuft on a bird's head

explanation.surface: A tiny bird sports a yellow feather.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is Europe's smallest bird, named for its yellow crown stripe.

clue.text: Sheep in flowerbed Elizabeth's favourite

parts.note: a border is a flowerbed along the edge of a lawn
Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was the favourite of Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A sheep has strayed into the late queen's prized garden bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was famously the favourite of Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Border Leicester is a British breed of long-wool sheep.

clue.text: Drawing farm vehicle with nothing on

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle
O is zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sketching an empty farm wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a humorous drawing or a preparatory sketch for a painting.

clue.text: Initially greeting smallest piglets with gruff sounds

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word greeting

parts.note: the runts are the smallest animals in a litter

explanation.surface: A farmer greets the tiniest piglets with gruff noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Grunts are low, rough noises, typical of pigs.

clue.text: American state colours appear in layers

parts.note: Rhode Island is the smallest US state
reds are colours

explanation.surface: A US state's flag colours appear in stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' looks like strata; it means hens that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhode Island Reds are a breed of chicken kept for eggs, so they are egg-producing birds.

clue.text: River in backward part of Germany

indicators.note: the word in is turned backward

parts.note: taken as written
Ger, the opening part of Germany, is its short form

explanation.surface: A river flows through a remote corner of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns IN into NI; GER, the start and short form of Germany, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is a major river of West Africa.

clue.text: Use hands to change protection against overheating

indicators.note: the letters of use hands are to change, i.e. be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to swap hands to stop a machine overheating.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is a parasol or awning that shields people from the sun's heat.

clue.text: Note a collection made up of teapot, cups and saucers

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a set is a collection

explanation.surface: A remark about what makes up a china service.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set is the matching china used for serving tea, made up of those items.

clue.text: Able to change to right agricultural equipment

indicators.note: the letters of the word able are told to change, i.e. be rearranged

explanation.surface: A capable farmer can switch over to the correct farm machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges ABLE into BALE; R for right follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A baler is a farm machine that compresses hay or straw into bales.

clue.text: Engineer groaned after reassembling harmonium for example

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: the word groaned is reassembled, its letters put together in a new order

explanation.surface: An engineer groaned after putting a harmonium back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reassembling' turns GROANED into EDORGAN, which follows RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium is one kind of keyboard instrument whose sound comes from vibrating free reeds.

clue.text: Randy Conservative hero comes between the French and us

indicators.note: the Conservative hero is placed between the two other pieces, the French article and us

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lustful Tory champion intrudes between the French and ourselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy here means lustful, a synonym for lewd and lascivious.

clue.text: Land on this planet

definitions.meaning: the ground or soil, as opposed to sea or sky
the world we live on, third from the Sun

explanation.surface: An instruction to touch down on our world.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both soil or ground and the name of our world.

clue.text: Legendary wizard's falcon

explanation.surface: The bird belonging to a fabled sorcerer.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to King Arthur's sorcerer and to a small bird of prey of moors and heath.

clue.text: Hampshire river (on the border) is the place to experiment

parts.note: the Test is a famous chalk trout river in Hampshire, a county in southern England
a bed is a garden border for flowers

explanation.surface: A stretch of river along a county boundary is used for trials.
explanation.walkthrough: The TEST is a river in Hampshire, southern England; 'border' is the garden kind, a flowerbed, giving BED.
explanation.definitionFit: A testbed is a facility or setting used for trying out new equipment or ideas.

clue.text: A bribe leads to permits, one pound less for single-storey houses

parts.note: a bung is a bribe in British slang

indicators.note: one pound is taken away, made less, from permits

parts.note: allows means permits
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A backhander secures building permits for bungalows at a pound off.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNG is British slang for a bribe; 'less' removes one L from ALLOWS to give ALOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bungalows are houses built on one floor only.

clue.text: Glaswegian liberated — no charge

parts.note: a person from Glasgow is a Scot
liberated means set free

explanation.surface: A man from Glasgow is released without being charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot-free means escaping without penalty, originally without paying a tax.

clue.text: Feline family start to smell Hazel perhaps

parts.note: a feline is a cat
kin are one's family

indicators.note: the start of the word smell gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A family of cats begins sniffing around someone called Hazel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' reads as a woman's name; it is the tree, whose dangling flowers are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazel trees bear long hanging flower spikes, so the tree is an example of a plant that has these.

clue.text: Reserve is en route, using underground tunnel

parts.note: a sub, short for substitute, is a reserve player
en route is on the way, giving way

explanation.surface: A substitute is on his way to the ground by tube.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a subway is a pedestrian passage under a road.

clue.text: Admirers put one among the birds

indicators.note: one is placed among, i.e. inside, the birds

parts.note: swans are birds
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Suitors place a single bird among a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Swains are young male lovers or suitors, in poetic usage.

clue.text: A petite person, but she has trapped a revolutionary trio

indicators.note: the word she holds, or has trapped, the trio inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of trio revolve, i.e. are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small woman has captured three revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges TRIO into ORTI, which 'has trapped' puts inside SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortie is an informal name for someone small.

clue.text: Hair on sister's head reveals tension

indicators.note: the head of the word sister's is its first letter

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A lock of hair on a sibling's head reveals strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is strain or pressure, mental or physical.

clue.text: Small shrub, yours once, is with me

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of 'your'
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned declaration that a small bush belongs to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a low aromatic woody plant used as a herb.

clue.text: Initially you and I led off with this product

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word you
the letters of led go off, i.e. are disordered

explanation.surface: You and I set off with our produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A yield is the amount produced, as of a crop.

clue.text: Programme produced by actors on East Anglian lake

indicators.note: the actors are put on, i.e. after, the lake

parts.note: the Broads are the lakes of Norfolk and Suffolk in East Anglia, eastern England
a cast is the group of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A show made by a troupe out on the Norfolk waters.
explanation.walkthrough: A broad is one of the shallow lakes of the Norfolk Broads in East Anglia, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast is a programme sent out on radio or television.

clue.text: New course of Trent near valley

indicators.note: the river's letters take a new course, i.e. are rearranged, along with near

explanation.surface: The River Trent changes direction near a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New course of' rearranges TRENT plus NEAR; the Trent is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: In geography a re-entrant is a small valley or hollow running into a hillside.

clue.text: Run away from underdeveloped area

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the words underdeveloped area

explanation.surface: Fleeing a poor region.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly, usually to marry.

clue.text: Shrubs for those with more seniority

definitions.meaning: small trees with white flowers and dark berries
older people or senior members of a group

explanation.surface: Bushes kept for the senior members.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a berry-bearing small tree and people who are older or senior.

clue.text: Carries on using press it's out of order

indicators.note: the letters of press and it's are placed out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps pushing a machine that is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue steadily despite difficulty.
